Anthropic docs, the trust-then-verify gap fix: 'Always provide verification (tests, scripts, screenshots). If you can't verify it, don't ship it.'

Anthropic docs on the kitchen-sink session: '/clear between unrelated tasks'; on repeated corrections: 'After two failed corrections, /clear and write a better initial prompt incorporating what you learned.'
Anthropic docs: 'Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!'

Anthropic large-codebases blog (the conflict): a rule to 'break every refactor into single-file changes may have helped an earlier model stay on track but would prevent a newer one from making coordinated cross-file edits.'
Anthropic docs on adversarial review: 'A reviewer prompted to find gaps will usually report some, even when the work is sound... Chasing every finding leads to over-engineering.'
Practitioner (chudi.dev): 'I shipped broken code three times in one week. The AI said "should work."' High-risk phrases to block: 'should work', 'probably fine', 'looks good'.

digitalapplied blog (self-reported claim): healthy skill libraries show top five skills at 60-80% of invocations; sprawled ones show top five at 90%+ with a long tail at zero — 'Curation is the work; collection is the trap.'

angle: Workflows from other AI coding tools (Cursor, Aider, Copilot, Windsurf, Cline) that transfer to refining features with Claude / Claude Code.
summary: Across Cursor, Aider, Copilot, Windsurf and Cline, the same handful of patterns recur and all map cleanly onto Claude Code primitives: (1) separate reasoning/planning from editing before any code is written (Aider architect mode, Cursor Plan Mode -> Claude plan mode + "explore, plan, code, commit"); (2) persist project context in checked-in markdown so the agent doesn't re-learn the codebase each session (Copilot copilot-instructions.md, Windsurf rules, Cline Memory Bank -> CLAUDE.md and skills); (3) capture repeated step-sequences as reusable commands (Windsurf workflows, Copilot prompt files -> Claude custom slash commands/skills); and (4) verify with a fresh, independent context rather than trusting the model that wrote the code (writer/reviewer split -> Claude verification subagents). The strongest, official-source claim is Anthropic's own best-practices guide, which independently prescribes plan mode, CLAUDE.md, subagents and adversarial review — confirming these borrowed patterns are first-class in Claude. Caveats: several techniques are explicitly experimental or promotional-source-only, and persistent-context files cost tokens and degrade behavior if bloated, so they must be pruned, not piled on.

techniques.name: Architect/Editor split: plan with a reasoning model, edit with another (Aider -> Claude plan mode)
techniques.description: Aider's experimental architect mode sends a request to a reasoning 'architect' model to describe the solution, then a separate 'editor' model turns that into formatted code edits, so neither model splits attention between solving and formatting. The page reports its top benchmark pairs as o1-preview architect + o1-mini editor at 85.0%, + deepseek at 85.0%, and + claude-3-5-sonnet at 82.7%. Transfers directly to Claude Code's plan mode: enter plan mode so Claude only reads/reasons, get a plan, then exit to implement. Anthropic's guide frames the same idea as 'Explore first, then plan, then code' to 'avoid solving the wrong problem.'
techniques.whenToUse: Research and Plan (separate reasoning from implementation before editing)

techniques.name: Plan-as-reviewable-artifact (Cursor Plan Mode / spec file -> Claude plan + SPEC.md)
techniques.description: Cursor Plan Mode analyzes the codebase, asks clarifying questions to surface blind spots, and emits a markdown plan with file paths and code references that you can 'tweak, refine, or rewrite right inside the editor' before execution ('pause, plan, proceed'). The transferable move is making the plan an editable artifact you review before code. In Claude Code, press Ctrl+G in plan mode to open the plan in your editor; or have Claude interview you with AskUserQuestion and 'write a complete spec to SPEC.md', then start a fresh session to implement it against that spec.
techniques.whenToUse: Plan (produce and human-review a written plan/spec before building)

techniques.name: Persistent project context as checked-in markdown (Copilot instructions / Windsurf rules / Cline Memory Bank -> CLAUDE.md)
techniques.description: Copilot uses .github/copilot-instructions.md (repo-wide) plus path-scoped *.instructions.md; Windsurf splits durable 'rules' (standards) from 'memories' (learned project context); Cline's Memory Bank methodology keeps six markdown files (projectbrief, productContext, activeContext, systemPatterns, techContext, progress) that the agent reads at session start and updates at session end. All transfer to Claude's CLAUDE.md, read at the start of every conversation; run /init to generate one, use the # key to append rules while working, and import other files with @path syntax. Place files at home/project/child-dir scope like Windsurf's global/project/component tiers.
techniques.whenToUse: Research/Build (give the agent durable, reusable context so it doesn't re-learn the codebase each session)

techniques.name: Keep the context file short and pruned, not exhaustive (Copilot/Windsurf caveat -> CLAUDE.md hygiene)
techniques.description: Copilot guidance: keep instructions to 'just a few sentences', list the stack/structure, and note 'an imperfect instructions file will deliver far more impact than nothing at all.' Windsurf enforces a hard 6,000-char per-rule and 12,000-char total limit specifically to keep context efficient. Anthropic echoes this as a failure mode: a bloated CLAUDE.md makes Claude 'ignore your actual instructions', so for each line ask 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?' and cut anything Claude can infer from code. Move sometimes-relevant detail into on-demand skills instead of loading it every turn.
techniques.whenToUse: Build (maintain the persistent-context file as a cost-bearing prompt, not a dumping ground)

techniques.name: Capture repeated step-sequences as reusable commands (Windsurf workflows / Copilot prompt files -> Claude slash commands & skills)
techniques.description: Windsurf's rule of thumb: 'If you do it more than once, make it a workflow' — a declarative, parameterized sequence (e.g. set up venv, install deps, lint, test, summarize) that references your rules. Copilot offers reusable .github/prompts/*.prompt.md. These transfer to Claude Code custom skills/slash commands: a .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md with steps (e.g. a fix-issue command that views the issue, edits, tests, lints, commits, opens a PR) invoked as /fix-issue 1234, with disable-model-invocation:true for side-effecting workflows you want to trigger manually.
techniques.whenToUse: Build/Share (turn a recurring refinement-to-PR routine into a one-command workflow)

techniques.name: Verify in a fresh, independent context (writer/reviewer split -> Claude verification subagent)
techniques.description: A recurring multi-tool pattern is using a second, clean context to grade work the first one produced, since a fresh model 'won't be biased toward code it just wrote.' Anthropic prescribes this directly: run an adversarial review in a subagent that sees only the diff and the criteria (e.g. the bundled /code-review skill, or 'use a subagent to review this diff against PLAN.md'), and pair it with a concrete pass/fail check (tests, build, screenshot) so the loop closes itself. Caveat from the same source: a reviewer asked to find gaps will usually find some even when the work is sound, so scope it to correctness/requirements to avoid over-engineering.
techniques.whenToUse: Verify (independent review + an executable check before declaring done)

notableQuotesOrExamples: Aider (verbatim): 'The Architect/Editor approach splits this into two inference steps, possibly using two different LLMs' — and the page labels it 'experimental support for using two models to complete each coding task.'
Aider benchmark (from aider.chat): top pairs were o1-preview architect + o1-mini editor 85.0%, + deepseek 85.0%, + claude-3-5-sonnet 82.7% (treat as the project's own self-reported numbers).
Windsurf practitioner heuristic (paraphrased from paulmduvall.com): 'If you do it more than once, make it a workflow'; Windsurf enforces 6,000 chars per rule and 12,000 chars across all active rules.
Copilot blog (paraphrased): 'an imperfect instructions file will deliver far more impact than nothing at all' — keep the project overview to a few sentences.

Cline Memory Bank uses six markdown files (projectbrief, productContext, activeContext, systemPatterns, techContext, progress); the agent reads all of them at the start of every task and you say 'update memory bank' to persist state at session end.
Anthropic best-practices (verbatim): 'Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!' and the test 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes? If not, cut it.'

Anthropic's four-phase loop maps the whole talk: Explore (plan mode, read-only) -> Plan ('Create a plan', Ctrl+G to edit it) -> Implement (exit plan mode, write tests, run suite) -> Commit (descriptive message + PR).
